tagline: Five hundred miles, volcano to volcano, from Lassen to Crater Lake.
intro: The byway starts with a loop through Lassen Volcanic National Park and around Lake Almanor, then heads north through Hat Creek and Burney to McCloud and Mount Shasta City. From Weed it follows US 97 up past Butte Valley to Dorris, crosses into Oregon between the Klamath wildlife refuges, runs beside Upper Klamath Lake and climbs to the rim of Crater Lake.

A loop by Medicine Lake goes out to Lava Beds National Monument, a country of lava tubes and the ground of the Modoc War of 1872 and 1873. Mount Shasta, at 14,179 feet, is the tallest volcano along the way.
season: For the Oregon end of the byway, ODOT's TripCheck gives June through October. Crater Lake's north entrance and rim drive close from November through May.

moments.title: Lassen Peak
moments.text: The road crosses a pass on the peak's shoulder. On May 22, 1915, the mountain threw ash 280 miles east, and the park was made partly to keep anyone from settling too close.

moments.title: Burney Falls
moments.text: Spring water out of porous basalt goes over a 129-foot fall at about 100 million gallons a day, and a loop trail from the overlook goes down to its foot.

moments.title: Crater Lake
moments.text: Clarence Dutton sounded it from his survey boat, the Cleetwood, with lead pipe and piano wire, and came close to what sonar found in 1959.

practical: The road through Lassen Volcanic National Park is usually closed in winter. Crater Lake's south entrance, on Oregon 62, is open year-round.
